title: La famille
subtitle: Family and possessive adjectives
source: Grammaire 1.1, pp. 65–66, and Vocabulaire: La famille

path.title: Révision du module
path.subtitle: Reading, listening, speaking and a mixed test

vocab.trick: Père, mère, frère all end in -ère. Père sounds like the start of “paternal”.
Mère: think “maternal”. The family that ends in -ère sticks together.
Frère: think “fraternity”, a group of brothers.
Sœur: think “sorority”, a group of sisters. Say “sir” with rounded lips.

vocab.tip: The l and s are silent: say “fiss”.
vocab.trick: Fils: a son “fills” the house. But the l and s are silent: “fiss”.
Fille: a filly is a young female horse. Fille = daughter, and also girl.
Mari: the one you marry. Husband = mari.
Femme: think “feminine”. It sounds like “fam”: she's your fam.

vocab.tip: Masculine or feminine. L' hides the gender before a vowel.
vocab.trick: Enfant: think “infant”. Same word, French accent.
Grand + père = grandfather, just like English. Grand for the older generation.
Grand + mère = grandmother. Same pattern as English.
Grands-parents: both words take an s, because there are two of them.

vocab.tip: Masculine, even though you only see l'.
vocab.trick: Oncle: “uncle” with an o. Masculine like every uncle.
Tante: picture your aunt in a tent. T-aunt-e.
Cousin: same as English. Add an e for a girl: cousine.
Cousine: cousin + e. In French, an e on the end often makes it feminine.
Beau means handsome. French calls in-laws “beautiful”: your beau-père is your handsome new father.
Belle means beautiful. Beau for men, belle for women: belle-mère.
Beau + frère: your “handsome brother”, the brother-in-law.
Belle + sœur: your “beautiful sister”, the sister-in-law.
Demi means half, like a demigod. Demi-frère = half brother.
Demi + sœur = half sister. Demi like a demitasse, a half cup.
Neveu sounds like “nephew” said fast.
Nièce: just like niece, with an accent.
Petit = little. Grandchildren are the “little” ones: petit-fils = grandson.
Petite-fille: “little daughter” = granddaughter. Grand going up, petit going down.
Petits-enfants: “little children” = grandchildren.
Époux: drop the é and squint: “spoux”, spouse.

vocab.tip: Feminine but starts with a vowel, so it's mon épouse.
vocab.trick: Épouse = spouse. Feminine but starts with a vowel, so mon épouse.

grammar.title: Possessive adjectives

teach.title: My, your, his, her…
teach.body: Possessive adjectives say whose something is: mon frère, ta sœur. They go right before the noun.

teach.title: Match the thing, not the owner
teach.body: The possessive agrees with the noun that is owned. Sa mère can mean his mother or her mother, because mère is feminine.

examples.en: Madame Martin looks at her book.

teach.title: The vowel rule
teach.body: Before a singular word starting with a vowel or a silent h, use mon, ton, son, even if the word is feminine. It's easier to say.

teach.title: Listen for the link
teach.body: A final s or n is pronounced when the next word starts with a vowel. mes enfants sounds like “mé-z-enfants”. mon ami sounds like “mon-n-ami”. But in mes filles and mon fils, the s and n stay quiet.

notes: Agree with the thing owned, not the owner: sa mère = his mother or her mother.
Before a vowel or silent h, use mon / ton / son, even for feminine nouns: mon amie.
Notre, votre, leur have no masculine or feminine form, only singular and plural.
Pronounce the s or n before a vowel: mes enfants (z), mon ami (n).

tricks.mon: The possessive is the noun's outfit: it dresses to match the noun, never the owner.
tricks.ma: Feminine noun, consonant start: ma, ta, sa. All end in a, like many feminine words.
tricks.mes: Plural? All three end in -es: mes, tes, ses. The s is for “several”.
tricks.vowel: Say “ma amie” out loud: two vowels crash. French hates that, so ma becomes mon. Mon amie flows.
tricks.sonsa: Ignore the owner. Ask: is the THING masculine or feminine? Marc's mother is still sa mère.
tricks.notre: Notre, votre: one thing. Nos, vos: many things. Short word for many, think “nos = nose-ful”.
tricks.leur: Leur = their, one thing. Leurs = their, many things. Add s for more, like English.

lines.fr: Mon, ma, mes : c'est à moi !
lines.en: My: it's mine!
lines.fa: مُن، ما، مِ : سِ تا موا!
lines.pr: mohn, mah, may: say tah MWAH!

lines.fr: Ton, ta, tes : c'est à toi !
lines.en: Your: it's yours!
lines.fa: تُن، تا، تِ : سِ تا توا!
lines.pr: tohn, tah, tay: say tah TWAH!

lines.fr: Son, sa, ses : à lui, à elle !
lines.en: His, her: his or hers!
lines.fa: سُن، سا، سِ : آ لویی، آ اِل!
lines.pr: sohn, sah, say: ah LWEE, ah EL!

lines.fr: Notre, nos : c'est à nous !
lines.en: Our: it's ours!
lines.fa: نُتر، نو : سِ تا نو!
lines.pr: NOH-truh, noh: say tah NOO!

lines.fr: Votre, vos : c'est à vous !
lines.en: Your: it's yours, all of you!
lines.fa: وُتر، وو : سِ تا وو!
lines.pr: VOH-truh, voh: say tah VOO!

lines.fr: Leur, leurs : c'est à eux !
lines.en: Their: it's theirs!
lines.fa: لُر، لُر : سِ تا اُ!
lines.pr: luhr, luhr: say tah UH!

exercises.why: Denise says tu to Jacqueline, and famille is feminine, so ta.
exercises.en: — Jacqueline, what is your family like?

exercises.text: — Est-ce que ___ frères et sœurs sont jeunes ?
exercises.why: Frères et sœurs is plural, so tes.
exercises.en: — Are your brothers and sisters young?

exercises.text: — Non, pas trop. ___ frère a 19 ans…
exercises.why: Jacqueline talks about her own brother. Frère is masculine, so mon.
exercises.en: — Not really. My brother is 19…

exercises.why: Sœurs is plural, so mes.
exercises.en: …and my sisters are 12 and 14.

exercises.text: — Est-ce que ___ grands-parents habitent dans la même ville que toi ?
exercises.why: Grands-parents is always plural, so tes.
exercises.en: — Do your grandparents live in the same town as you?

exercises.why: Grand-mère is feminine and starts with a consonant, so ma.
exercises.en: — My grandmother lives with us…

exercises.why: Grand-père is masculine, so mon.
exercises.en: …but my grandfather has died.

exercises.text: — Est-ce que ___ mère est une personne active ?
exercises.why: Asking Jacqueline (tu) about her mother: mère is feminine, so ta.
exercises.en: — Is your mother an active person?

exercises.why: Her job: job is masculine, so son, even though the mother is a woman.
exercises.en: — Yes. With her job…

exercises.why: Enfants is plural, so ses.
exercises.en: …and her children, she is very busy.

exercises.why: Frère is masculine, talking to tu, so ton.
exercises.en: — Does your brother still live at home?

exercises.why: His own apartment: appartement is masculine, so son.
exercises.en: — No, he has his own apartment.

exercises.text: Il y a dix étudiants dans ___ classe.
exercises.why: Classe is singular, so notre.
exercises.en: There are ten students in our class.

exercises.why: Camarades is plural, so nos.
exercises.en: Our classmates are outgoing.

exercises.why: One teacher, so notre.
exercises.en: Our teacher is named Madame Dubois.

exercises.why: Devoirs is plural, so nos.
exercises.en: Our homework is easy.

exercises.text: Évelyne writes: “Mes parents sont jeunes et énergiques.” Report it: ___ parents sont jeunes et énergiques.
exercises.why: Her parents, plural: ses.
exercises.en: “My parents are young and energetic.” → Her parents are young and energetic.

exercises.text: “Ma sœur Madeleine est très amusante.” Report it: ___ sœur Madeleine est très amusante.
exercises.why: Her sister, feminine: sa.
exercises.en: “My sister Madeleine is very funny.” → Her sister Madeleine is very funny.

exercises.text: Rewrite as Évelyne's friend would say it: “Mon père travaille avec mon oncle.”
exercises.answer: Son père travaille avec son oncle.
exercises.why: Her father and her uncle: both masculine, so son and son.
exercises.en: “My father works with my uncle.” → Her father works with her uncle.

exercises.text: “Notre maison est très vieille et très grande.” Report it: ___ maison est très vieille et très grande.
exercises.why: Our house becomes their house: leur (one house, so no s).
exercises.en: “Our house is very old and very big.” → Their house is very old and very big.

exercises.text: Rewrite as Évelyne's friend would say it: “Mon amie Sabrine est très intelligente.”
exercises.answer: Son amie Sabrine est très intelligente.
exercises.why: Amie is feminine, but it starts with a vowel, so son.
exercises.en: “My friend Sabrine is very smart.” → Her friend Sabrine is very smart.

lines.fr: Voici une photo de ma famille.
lines.en: Here is a photo of my family.
lines.fa: وواسی یون فُتو دُ ما فامی
lines.pr: vwah-SEE oon foh-TOH duh mah fah-MEE-y

lines.fr: À gauche, c'est mon père, Gaston, et ma mère, Colette.
lines.en: On the left, that's my father, Gaston, and my mother, Colette.
lines.fa: آ گُش، سِ مُن پِر، گاستُن، اِ ما مِر، کُلِت
lines.pr: ah GOHSH, say mohn PEHR, gahs-TOHN, ay mah MEHR, koh-LET

lines.fr: Mon frère s'appelle Pompon. Il a cinq ans.
lines.en: My brother is named Pompon. He is five.
lines.fa: مُن فرِر ساپِل پُنپُن. ایلا سَنکان
lines.pr: mohn FREHR sah-PEL pohn-POHN. ee-LAH san-KAHN

lines.fr: Ma sœur, Praline, a sept ans.
lines.en: My sister, Praline, is seven.
lines.fa: ما سُر، پرالین، آ سِتان
lines.pr: mah SUHR, prah-LEEN, ah seh-TAHN

lines.fr: Au centre, ce sont mes grands-parents. Ma grand-mère adore les chats !
lines.en: In the middle are my grandparents. My grandmother loves cats!
lines.fa: اُ سانتر، سُ سُن مِ گران‌پاران. ما گران‌مِر آدُر لِ شا
lines.pr: oh SAHN-truh, suh sohn may grahn-pah-RAHN. mah grahn-MEHR ah-DOR lay SHAH

lines.fr: Mon oncle Félix est là aussi, avec sa femme et leurs enfants.
lines.en: My uncle Félix is there too, with his wife and their children.
lines.fa: مُنُنکل فِلیکس اِ لا اُسی، آوِک سا فام اِ لُرزانفان
lines.pr: moh-NOHN-kluh fay-LEEKS ay LAH oh-SEE, ah-VEK sah FAHM ay luhr-zahn-FAHN

lines.fr: Leurs enfants sont mes cousins.
lines.en: Their children are my cousins.
lines.fa: لُرزانفان سُن مِ کوزَن
lines.pr: luhr-zahn-FAHN sohn may koo-ZAN

questions.q: Comment s'appelle le frère de Minou ?

lines.fr: Sami, tu as des frères et sœurs ?
lines.en: Sami, do you have brothers and sisters?
lines.fa: سامی، تو آ دِ فرِر اِ سُر؟
lines.pr: sah-MEE, tü ah day FREHR ay SUHR?

lines.fr: Oui, j'ai un frère et deux sœurs. Mon frère a dix ans.
lines.en: Yes, I have a brother and two sisters. My brother is ten.
lines.fa: وی، ژِ اَن فرِر اِ دُ سُر. مُن فرِر آ دیزان
lines.pr: WEE, zhay uhn FREHR ay duh SUHR. mohn FREHR ah dee-ZAHN

lines.fr: Et tes sœurs ?
lines.en: And your sisters?
lines.fa: اِ تِ سُر؟
lines.pr: ay tay SUHR?

lines.fr: Mes sœurs ont huit et neuf ans. Et toi ?
lines.en: My sisters are eight and nine. And you?
lines.fa: مِ سُر زُن ویت اِ نُوان. اِ توا؟
lines.pr: may SUHR zohn WEET ay nuh-VAHN. ay TWAH?

lines.fr: Moi, je n'ai pas de frère, mais j'ai une demi-sœur. Sa mère est ma belle-mère.
lines.en: I don't have a brother, but I have a half sister. Her mother is my stepmother.
lines.fa: موا، ژُ نِ پا دُ فرِر، مِ ژِ یون دُمی‌سُر. سا مِر اِ ما بِل‌مِر
lines.pr: MWAH, zhuh nay pah duh FREHR, may zhay oon duh-mee-SUHR. sah MEHR ay mah bel-MEHR

lines.fr: Et tes grands-parents ?
lines.en: And your grandparents?
lines.fa: اِ تِ گران‌پاران؟
lines.pr: ay tay grahn-pah-RAHN?

lines.fr: Ma grand-mère habite chez nous. Mon grand-père habite à Lyon avec mon oncle.
lines.en: My grandmother lives with us. My grandfather lives in Lyon with my uncle.
lines.fa: ما گران‌مِر آبیت شِ نو. مُن گران‌پِر آبیت آ لیُن آوِک مُنُنکل
lines.pr: mah grahn-MEHR ah-BEET shay NOO. mohn grahn-PEHR ah-BEET ah lee-OHN ah-VEK moh-NOHN-kluh

questions.hint: How many sisters does Sami have?

questions.q: Quel âge a le frère de Sami ?

sentences.fr: J'ai un frère et une sœur.
sentences.en: I have a brother and a sister.
sentences.fa: ژِ اَن فرِر اِ یون سُر
sentences.pr: zhay uhn FREHR ay oon SUHR

sentences.en: My sister is ten years old.

sentences.fr: Mon amie Agnès a un fils.
sentences.en: My friend Agnès has a son.

sentences.fr: Mes neveux ont six et huit ans.
sentences.en: My nephews are six and eight.
sentences.fa: مِ نُوُ زُن سیس اِ ویتان
sentences.pr: may nuh-VUH zohn SEESS ay wee-TAHN
